title: Context economics: quick annotations & experiment sketch
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Quick brain-dump after reading a mix of papers + a couple of blog threads about episodic compression, prefix caching, and low-bit KV behavior.
- Goal: produce 2 cheap, fast experiments that give actionable knobs for Redwood Optimize (batching/cache/quant recommendations).

High-level takeaways (rough):
1) Small prefix cache hits give outsized latency wins for multi-turn assistants, but hit-rate is very sensitive to chunking strategy.
   - note: naive fixed-length chunking loses on pivot phrases; semantic chunk boundaries help hit-rate ~+10-20%.
2) Quantized KVs (4-bit / 8-bit) often keep generation quality for repeated prefixes but degrade for rare tokens -> useful for tail-suppression heuristics.
3) Episodic compression (learned or heuristic) best when average session length > 2k tokens; otherwise overhead of compress/decompress can dominate.
4) Batching + small cache yields compounding cost-savings but increases p95 latency unpredictably; need SLO-aware batching policy.

Questions / hypotheses to test (quick):
- H1: For chat assistants with average turn=80 tokens and session length≈1200 tokens, semantic chunking + 8-bit quantized KV reduces per-token GPU work by ~18% with <1% quality regressions on retrieval prompts.
- H2: Ephemeral compression (lightweight LZW-style tuned for token IDs) can beat neural compression for compress/decompress latency on CPU if compression ratio >1.5x.

Experiment sketch A: "semantic prefix cache + quantized KV" (2-week lightweight run) - Objective: measure hit-rate/latency/tradeoffs for semantic vs fixed chunking when storing recent prefixes in cache and serving from 8-bit KV.
- Workload: replay 5k real-production sessions sampled from last 30 days (sanitized), each session ~1k tokens.
- Variants: fixed-128 chunking baseline; semantic-breakpoints (BPE/encoder boundary heuristic); semantic + merge-short-chunks.
- KV formats: float16 baseline, 8-bit symmetric quant, 4-bit (optional for tail tests).
- Metrics: cache hit-rate, p50/p95 generation latency, tokens-per-second, top-1 edit-distance on target completions (proxy for quality), GPU utilization, cost-per-1M-tokens.
- Success criteria: >=15% cost reduction vs baseline with <2% drop in quality proxy.
- Data/infra notes: use staging Redwood Dedicated pool (small test queue), enable trace sampling for correctness checks.

Experiment sketch B: "lightweight episodic compression benchmark"
- Objective: compare neural vs byte-level vs simple token-id run-length/LZW-style compressors for storage+decode latency & net cost.
- Workload: 2k long sessions (3k-8k tokens), test compress/decompress on CPU and GPU paths (where applicable).
- Variants: no-compress baseline; zstd tuned; toy run-length on repeating tokens; neural autoencoder (small) that compresses blocks of 512 tokens.
- Metrics: compression ratio, compress latency (ms/block), decompress latency (ms/block), net end-to-end generation latency impact, memory footprint, cost-model delta.
- Quick win idea: if simple token-id RLE yields >1.6x on typical assistant sessions and decompress <6ms/block, ship as "ephemeral compression v0" for Dedicated.

Notes to self / operational gotchas:
- Need to instrument prefix boundary alignment in sampling pipeline; small off-by-one bugs change hit-rate dramatically.
- Watch out for magical interaction between continuous batching and prefix cache eviction: batching increases effective cache TTL (requests batched may reuse same KV slice), skewing measurements.
- Quality proxy: top-1 edit-distance is cheap but misses hallucination differences; include a tiny human-annotated eval set (100 sessions) for final check.

Micro-actions (next 7 working days):
- Day 1: finalize sampling query and anonymization step (Rita). add simple filter to exclude PII.
- Day 2: implement semantic chunker (Kenji) — rough heuristic using sentence+punct boundary + token window.
- Day 3: wire 8-bit quant path in staging runtime (small PR) and a flag to toggle per-stream KV format.
- Day 4: run smoke tests (100 sessions) and sanity-check quality proxies.
- Days 5-7: run full A/B for Experiment A on small Dedicated pool; collect traces and start analysis.

Loose thoughts / brainstorming fragments:
- What if cache prefers "recent unchanged embeddings" rather than token-prefixes? That could be cheaper for some dialogue styles.
- Consider a hybrid TTL + usage-count eviction that promotes conversational anchors (user IDs/page IDs).
- Edge case: highly personal prompts (long user rolodex) — compressing might leak structure; need to ensure no patterns that correlate to identity remain in compressed artifacts (privacy review).

References skimmed while writing (quick):
- Semantic chunking blog thread: https://example.blog/semantic-chunking (skim)
- "KV Compression for LLMs" (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08851
- Zstd perf notes and settings (internal confluence): CONFLUENCE-Compression-Notes

Open to feedback: prioritization between A (likely fast wins) vs B (higher engineering cost, bigger upside for very long sessions).

TODO (short):
- [ ] Create JIRA tickets for sampling + anonymization (JIRA-4521)
- [ ] Draft perf dashboard (p50/p95/cost-per-1M) for tracking experiments
- [ ] Pull small human eval set and define rubric

End notes: keeping this intentionally rough. Will tidy into a playbook if Experiment A returns clean savings.

- anika (notes to self: move completed checklist to Confluence page and drop link once polished)
